newsitem.title: FRANCE: Reuters French Advertising & Media Digest-June 23.
newsitem.headline: Reuters French Advertising & Media Digest-June 23.

text.p: REUTERS FRENCH ADVERTISING & MEDIA DIGEST
-------------- June 23, 1997 ------------ News from Reuters and the French press on Advertising, Marketing, Media, the Internet, Brand-name Products and People News.
ADVERTISING & MARKETING:
PARIS - The French riviera resort of Cannes becomes the judging
ground for a vast annual festival of advertising spots and
posters, with
4,500 commercials and 6,000 posters vying for the coveted Lion
awards.(Reuter)
PARIS - Michele Bleustein-Blanchet, daughter of the deceased
founder of French ad agency Publicis, who wants to sell her
stake in the
firm, says in an interview that there is a conflict between
Publicis
shareholders over the company's shareholding structure. (Les
Echos)
MEDIA & THE INTERNET
PARIS - France's new culture and communication
minister Catherine Trautmann says she will present a draft law
to reform
the broadcasting sector in autumn.(Reuter)
MUNICH - German media firm Leo Kirch has agreed to buy an extra
37.5 percent stake in pay TV channel Premiere from its current
French holder, Canal Plus, the German magazine Focus said in its
weekend edition.(Reuter)
BRAND-NAME PRODUCTS & MARKETS:
PARIS - The launch of a variant of Pernod Ricard's Orangina
fizzy drink, a blood orange Orangina, has slightly boosted the
brand's share in a shrinking market, Orangina chairman Jacques
Pfister says.(Reuter)
PARIS - Shares in luxury goods group LVMH Moet Hennessy Louis
Vuitton rebound after losing ground since it began buying Grand
Metropolitan
stock last week.
Some analysts see value in the LVMH proposal to group the three
companies' drinks businesses and spin off the brewing, canned
vegetable and
fast-food operations.(Reuter)
PARIS - Few French people would want to do without a freezer in
the kitchen, but nearly half would be happy to live without a
dishwasher,
according to a poll by IPSOS for monthly magazine Cuisines et
Vins de
France.(Reuter)
ABIDJAN - Ivorian President Henri Konan Bedie tells visiting
French confectioners to unite against a European Union proposal
which
would allow wider use of non-cocoa fats in chocolate.(Reuter)
Paris Editorial, Sue Landau
